proof.criterion: A1 — a stalled session reads unresponsive with its last registration, the default list omits it and include=unresponsive answers it, both answers survive a listener restart and agree across two listeners, SIGCONT returns it to live, and a raise and a rollback of the bucket's maximum age reach both running listeners within 2 minutes
proof.surface: the issue pod: a real Oh My Pi session on this branch's @sjawhar/pi-envoy build, against two listeners and a nats-server built from this branch, stopped with SIGSTOP and continued with SIGCONT
proof.command: LEGION_E2E_MODEL_BASE_URL=<the pod's model gateway> LEGION_E2E_MODEL_KEY_FILE=<its key file> LEGION_E2E_MODEL_ID=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 LEGION_E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5 ENVOY_SESSION_STATES_PG_DSN="$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN" bash scripts/e2e/envoy-session-states.sh
proof.observed: PASS stalled-session-reads-unresponsive and PASS max-age-change-reaches-both-listeners. 'SIGSTOPped Oh My Pi (pid 42500); its last registration was 1793501311230' / 'stalled since 1793501311230: unresponsive on both listeners, and across listener B's restart' / 'SIGCONT returned it to live on both listeners' / 'the raise to 2h reached both running listeners' /healthz' / 'registered ses_ess_maxage_41764 after the raise; stalling it 420s, past the shipping maximum age' / 'the rollback to 5m reached both listeners, and the session stalled past it then reads gone'. Evidence /legion/scratch/tmp/ess-head/evidence.
proof.negativeControl: The same rig at a gone horizon collapsed to the live window reports the stalled session gone instead: 'ses_stalled_732 still reads gone, not unresponsive, at the deadline' (run recorded while building the committed rig, packages/envoy-client/test/session-stall.ts). The run's own in-band control is the rollback half: once the bucket's maximum age is back at the shipping 5 minutes, the session stalled past it reads gone, not unresponsive.

proof.criterion: A2 — through a NATS outage two stalled sessions stay unresponsive and keep their role and issue claims
proof.surface: the issue pod: the run's own nats-server stopped for 180 s with two stalled real sessions around it
proof.observed: PASS bus-outage-keeps-claims. 'stopped NATS for 180s with both sessions stalled and both claims held' / 'after a 180s bus outage both sessions are unresponsive and keep the role claim and the issue claim'.
proof.negativeControl: The claims are read from envoy_roles and from Dispatch after the outage rather than before it, so a release during the stop would show as a missing holder; the check fails on exactly that. Before this change the role-claim reaper released a holder whose record the bucket no longer held, which is the state a 180 s outage leaves.

proof.criterion: A3 — a send to an unresponsive session is accepted with recipient_state, a mention and a message stored for it each arrive once after SIGCONT with no delivery failure, and a send to an unresponsive session that receives on a serving port is refused naming the state
proof.surface: the issue pod: the stalled Oh My Pi session's own transcript, and a real OpenCode session on this branch's @sjawhar/opencode-legion-envoy build
proof.command: the same script, checks send-to-stalled-session-is-stored, stored-deliveries-arrive-once and send-to-serving-port-is-refused
proof.observed: PASS on all three. 'the send was accepted with recipient_state unresponsive and last_seen 1793501555440' / 'the mention and the direct message each arrived once after SIGCONT; the role publish was refused with the claim kept' / 'a send to the stalled OpenCode session on port 35585 was refused 404 naming unresponsive'. The arrival count is read from the session's own transcript as delivery cards, the way packages/pi-envoy/extensions/card-delivery-omp.test.ts counts them.
proof.negativeControl: The role publish in the same check is the control for the refusal half: it is refused while the claim stays with its unresponsive holder. For the arrival half, the check requires exactly one card per delivery, so a second copy fails it — the count that first read 6 (occurrences of the marker, including the model's own thinking) is what made this check red before the rig was corrected.

proof.criterion: A4 — five lookups, a publish, a direct nats publish and a reaper pass leave an unresponsive holder's claim and claimed_at unchanged, each answering 404 holder_lapsed with holder_state unresponsive, last_seen and claim_released false, and a soft claim takes the role with and without a named predecessor
proof.surface: the issue pod: the stalled Oh My Pi session holding a real role claim, read back from the envoy_roles bucket
proof.observed: PASS role-claim-survives-lookups. 'five lookups, a publish, a direct nats publish and a reaper pass left ess-lookup-41764 with ses_ess_lookup_holder_41764, claimed_at unchanged' / 'a soft claim took the role, with and without a named predecessor'.
proof.negativeControl: claimed_at is compared before and after, so a release and re-claim fails the check even though the holder would read the same. The committed listener test TestLookupsAndAReaperPassLeaveAStalledHoldersRoleClaimExactlyAsItWas pins the same property, and a listener built without the state test releases the claim on the first lookup.

proof.criterion: A5 — another agent's claim and release are refused naming the holder's state and since when, and dispatch read --issue prints unresponsive since <t> with the takeable time
proof.surface: the issue pod: a real Dispatch server over the run's own database, and a second agent session's dispatch claim against the stalled holder
proof.observed: PASS issue-claim-refuses-the-stalled-holder. 'Claimed by: rig ses_ess_issue_holder_41764 since 2026-11-01T02:56:53.082182Z · unresponsive since 2026-11-01T02:56:52.778Z, takeable at 2026-11-01T03:16:52.778Z'.
proof.negativeControl: The check drives the take as a second agent and requires the refusal; a server that read the stalled holder as gone would let the take through. The browser suite's claim-unresponsive.e2e.ts is the same property on the page a person reads.

proof.criterion: A6 — SIGKILL leaves a session unresponsive until the gone horizon and gone after it, the reaper releases its role claim only then, a clean stop is gone at once including with a registration in flight, a new session id leaves the old one gone at once, and claude --resume within 15 minutes gets its topics back; the SIGKILL-to-gone latency is reported as a measured number
proof.surface: the issue pod: a real Oh My Pi session and a real Claude Code session on this branch's packages/claude-envoy build, each killed under its own process session, plus /clear, claude --resume and new_session
proof.observed: PASS gone-only-past-the-horizon. 'SIGKILL-to-gone latency: 90s (gone horizon 90s, a reaper pass every 10s)' / 'the role claim was released only once its holder was gone' / 'a clean SIGTERM left the OpenCode session gone at once, its registration still settling' / '/clear left the old id gone at once, and claude --resume brought its topics back' / 'new_session left 01a19502-2fb9-7507-b317-cb5a923f4f35 gone at once and registered 01a1950b-f0ef-77bf-90e9-e7552248719e'. The measured latency is 90 s against a 90 s gone horizon with a 10 s reaper period: the kill is detected at the horizon, not before it, which is the rule.
proof.negativeControl: The check reads the role claim before the horizon as well as after it and fails if it is released early, so an implementation that releases on a missed heartbeat fails it. The clean-stop half is the control for the kill half: the same session ended cleanly is gone at once rather than after 90 s.

proof.criterion: A7 — a re-read keeps every row and drops only the unfound ones, a read that times out removes nothing and is started again, the lists answer 503 with Retry-After while the copy cannot be served and every Dispatch view says refilling, and envoy_active_sessions publishes no sample during that 503
proof.surface: the listener with a real NATS whose bucket stream is recreated, and the Dispatch browser suite against a built dashboard
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/listener/ -run 'Refill' ./internal/kvwatch/ ./internal/session/ ./internal/store/; cd packages/dispatch && bun test
proof.observed: ok internal/kvwatch, ok internal/session, ok internal/store, and packages/dispatch 3008 pass 0 fail at this head. This criterion is dispatch://INFRA-261's four acceptance bullets, carried whole by this branch's first commit (the merge of sjawhar/legion#2238); its behaviour is the refilling 503 and the delta-FIFO re-read the merge brings in.
proof.negativeControl: The committed rig's maximum-age choice is the control for the re-read rule: at a bucket maximum age below the gone horizon the stalled record is removed before unresponsive can be read, which reads as gone — the defect itself — and the rig sets the age 30× the horizon so that it is the state model, not the bucket, that decides.

proof.criterion: A8 — in a real session of each of the three plugins each tool shows the state and last_seen, ending a session makes it gone at once including OpenCode's session.deleted and a SIGTERM to the serve, the four counters are on /metrics, and no skill tells an agent to read a process, a pane or a transcript to judge liveness
proof.surface: the issue pod: a real session of each of Oh My Pi, Claude Code and OpenCode on this branch's plugin builds; /metrics on the run's listener; grep over the tree
proof.command: the same script, check every-plugin-shows-the-state; and grep -rn 'ps -eo\|tmux pane\|transcript modification time' skills/leading-a-work-stream/SKILL.md
proof.observed: PASS every-plugin-shows-the-state. 'all three hosts showed the peer's state and its last_seen' / 'session.deleted left ses_e6af33e0fffeE6Y5AO9Ks3bC1U gone at once' / 'a SIGTERM to the serve left its session gone at once'. The grep returns nothing.
proof.negativeControl: This check is what found the OpenCode defect rather than confirming it: at the previous head it failed, and a probe plugin showed OpenCode delivers session.status, session.idle, session.diff and message.part.delta to a plugin's event hook and never session.deleted, so the deleted session kept being heartbeated — 16 subscribes and 0 unsubscribes for the deleted id in the listener's log. The fix is the heartbeat asking the serve for each tracked session; the check is green only because the product changed.

trickyParts: The branch's first commit is the merge of sjawhar/legion#2238 (dispatch://INFRA-261) into main: 54 conflicted files, two designs rewriting the same subsystems. That is where a silent revert would hide and it is the reviewer's first job. One was caught and corrected during the merge: INFRA-261's repair.go came back carrying the base's behaviour, which main had deliberately removed, so main's refinement (unrepairedDelay = bus.RepairGrace, one report point, no repairFailedReason) was restored.

Two forward merges were needed because GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING, each with its fingerprint comment on the pull request. The second carried sjawhar/legion#2592 (dispatch://INFRA-404), whose soft-claim rule had to compose with this one rather than replace it: a soft claim now supersedes a holder that is not live AND, where a predecessor is named, only within one client instance. Neither condition was dropped.

The role-lane answer for an unresponsive holder is 404 holder_lapsed, which is the approved spec read literally; the architect confirmed it against sjawhar/legion#2588, which is changing the same answer for a released claim. An unresponsive holder is a retained claim and must stay one — that is the hinge the two changes meet on.
A session's state is computed from the record's UpdatedAt and never from cache membership. Any later change that reintroduces a membership test reintroduces this defect.
deviations: The plan had T1 add InstanceMatches. It does not: the dispatch://INFRA-404 tree owns that name in its own internal/session/instance.go and merged first, so defining it here would have been a duplicate. Agreed with that tree's implementer before the fact.

The clean stop is sent by the daemon, not by the worker shim as R7 words it: no shimwire frame carries a session id, an Envoy URL or an Envoy token, and the shim already commits nine of its ten stop-grace seconds. The daemon holds all three, learns of the exit event-driven, and also covers a SIGKILLed shim and a lost pod. Recorded as departure 1 of the plan and accepted by the architect.

A1's raise-and-rollback clause is proved for a session stalled after the raise, not before it, because raising a bucket's maximum age restores no key JetStream already removed. Recorded as departure 2 and accepted by the architect.

The live window is a setting (ENVOY_SESSION_LIVE_WINDOW), which the spec's Values section lists only for the gone horizon, the reaper intervals and the claim protection. Without it each of A1 to A6 costs 7 minutes of wall clock. Recorded as departure 4.
A1 to A6 and A8 are proved on two surfaces, not one: the committed rig for regressions and the pod E2E for acceptance. Recorded as departure 3.

R9 and A9 — the theorem-labs/agent-infra pins and the raise of the production bucket's maximum age to 2 hours — are the architect's three child issues, not this pull request. This ships at the shipping 5-minute maximum age with ENVOY_SESSION_MAX_AGE unset.

The three Dispatch skills are gated at 2,000 words and stood at 1,995, so the three states went into the sentence that already named a lapsed claim rather than into a paragraph of their own. The rule in full is in skills/envoy and in the tool descriptions.

The role-claim reaper's period was a fixed five minutes that no setting moved, while packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md already promised it followed ENVOY_SESSION_REAP_INTERVAL. It now does, at the same default. This was not in the plan; it is a defect the proof found.
openQuestions: packages/daemon/internal/claudelaunch has the same CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA split the pod proof hit: MCPConfig sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=<configDir>/envoy-plugin-data for the channel server while Environment(configDir) exports nothing, and Claude Code sets that variable for a hook itself. So a pod's Claude Code worker should never adopt a /clear the way the proof's session did until that is reconciled. Found while fixing the proof's own copy of the same mistake; outside this issue's scope and reported rather than changed.
discoveredComplexity: The first full pod run was 6 of 10. Four were rig defects — a delivery count that counted every line naming the marker including the model's own thinking, a mention posted as @text rather than through Dispatch's mentions field, an OpenCode plugin that never loaded because the rig pointed at the checkout where prepack stages the skills directory, and a SIGSTOP that hit OpenCode's Node launcher rather than the serve it spawns. Two were product defects the proof found and this change fixes: OpenCode never delivers session.deleted to a plugin's event hook, so a deleted session kept being heartbeated, and the role-claim reaper's period did not follow its listener's setting.

The simplify pass found three more defects rather than style: the OpenCode plugin passed a bare session id to an unregisterSession that now takes an object, so every delete went to /v1/sessions/undefined; the session reaper's stored-message count walked the whole three-day subject history per reaped record with a per-record rather than per-pass budget; and Dispatch could not deliver to a role whose holder was unresponsive, because its client turned the listener's correct 404 into a refusal when resolving needs the holder's capabilities.
